title: Understanding VPNs: How They Work, Why They Matter, and Their Limitations
author: Chulanka Lakmana Thabrew
description: In today’s digital world, privacy and security have become major concerns for internet users. Whether you’re browsing from home, using public Wi-Fi, or accessing online services while traveling, your internet activity can potentially be monitored by various parties. This is where Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) come into play. What is a VPN? A Virtual Private Network (VPN) is a technology that creates a secure, encrypted connection between your device and a remote server operated by the VPN provider. Instead of connecting directly to websites and online services, your internet traffic first passes through the VPN server. This process hides your real IP address and encrypts your data, making it more difficult for third parties to monitor your online activities. Photo by NASA on Unsplash How Does a VPN Work? When you connect to a VPN: Your device establishes an encrypted tunnel to the VPN server. All internet traffic is sent through this tunnel. The VPN server forwards your requests to websites and online services. Responses are sent back through the encrypted tunnel to your device. As a result, websites see the VPN server’s IP address instead of your actual IP address. Key Benefits of Using a VPN 1. Enhanced Privacy VPNs hide your real IP address, making it harder for websites, advertisers, and internet service providers (ISPs) to track your browsing habits. 2. Improved Security Encryption protects your data from hackers, especially when using public Wi-Fi networks in airports, hotels, or cafes. 3. Secure Remote Access Many organizations use VPNs to allow employees to access company resources from remote locations securely. 4. Reduced ISP Monitoring Without a VPN, your ISP can often see the websites you visit. A VPN encrypts this traffic, limiting what the ISP can observe. 5. Bypassing Geographic Restrictions VPNs can allow users to connect through servers in different countries, which may help access region-specific content and services. Common VPN Protocols Different VPN protocols offer different balances between speed, security, and compatibility. OpenVPN One of the most widely used VPN protocols. It is open-source, highly secure, and supported on many platforms. 2. WireGuard A modern VPN protocol known for its simplicity, high performance, and strong security. 3. IKEv2/IPSec Popular on mobile devices due to its ability to reconnect quickly when switching between networks. 4. L2TP/IPSec An older protocol that combines Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol with IPSec encryption. Limitations of VPNs While VPNs provide many benefits, they are not a complete privacy solution. Slower Connection Speeds Trust in the VPN Provider Not Complete Anonymity Cost High-quality VPN services typically require a subscription fee. VPN Use Cases VPNs are commonly used for: Protecting data on public Wi-Fi. Secure remote work. Online privacy enhancement. Accessing geographically distributed services. Protecting sensitive communications. Choosing a VPN When selecting a VPN service, consider: Security protocols offered. No-logs policy. Server locations. Connection speed. Device compatibility. Independent security audits. Photo by FlyD on Unsplash The Future of VPN Technology As privacy concerns continue to grow, VPN technology is evolving. Modern protocols such as WireGuard are improving performance while maintaining strong security. At the same time, governments, organizations, and privacy advocates continue to debate the balance between security, privacy, and internet regulation. Conclusion VPNs have become an essential tool for improving online privacy and security. By encrypting internet traffic and masking IP addresses, they help protect users from various online threats. However, VPNs are not a magic solution for complete anonymity. Understanding both their strengths and limitations allows users to make informed decisions about protecting their digital lives. In an era where data has become one of the world’s most valuable resources, VPNs represent an important step toward a safer and more private internet experience.

title: Understanding Git Licenses: Why They Matter & How to Choose the Right One
author: Chulanka Lakmana Thabrew
description: When you publish code on git based platforms like GitHub, you’re not just sharing code, you’re defining how others can use, modify, and distribute it. That’s where licenses come in. Whether you’re building a side project, contributing to open source, or launching a startup, understanding licenses is essential. 📌 What is a License? A software license is a legal document that specifies how your code can be used by others. Without a license, Your code is legally protected by default copyright and others can’t legally use, modify or distribute it. No license = No permission Photo by Bernd 📷 Dittrich on Unsplash 🤔 Why Do You Need a License? Adding a license isn’t just a formality , it has real impact. Key reasons: Clarifies usage rights (what others can and cannot do) Encourages collaboration (people feel safe contributing) Protects you legally Defines attribution rules Prevents misuse of your code 📚 Types of Licenses Licenses generally fall into three categories: 1. 🟢 Permissive Licenses These are flexible and business-friendly. Examples: MIT License Very simple and widely used Allows reuse with minimal restrictions Requires only attribution Apache License 2.0 Similar to MIT but includes patent protection Good for larger/open-source projects BSD License Minimal restrictions Similar to MIT but slightly more formal 👉 Best for: Maximum adoption and flexibility 2. 🔴 Copyleft Licenses These are restrictive and protective. Examples: GPL (General Public License) Requires derivatives to also be open source Strong “share-alike” rule AGPL Even stricter than GPL Covers web services too 👉 Best for: Ensuring your code stays open forever 3. 🟡 Weak Copyleft Licenses A balance between permissive and restrictive. Examples: LGPL Allows linking with proprietary software Modifications must remain open 👉 Best for: Libraries and frameworks 📄 GitHub License Templates GitHub Licenses provides built-in license templates to make things easy. When creating a repository: You can select a license directly GitHub auto-generates a LICENSE file Popular templates include: MIT Apache 2.0 GPL v3 BSD 3-Clause 👉 This helps beginners avoid legal complexity ⚙️ How to Add a License to Your Project Method 1: Using GitHub UI Go to your repository Click “Add file” → “Create new file” Name it LICENSE Click “Choose a license template” Select and commit Method 2: Manually Create a file named LICENSE Copy license text (e.g., from opensource.org) Replace Your name and year Commit the file 🧠 How to Choose the Right License Ask yourself: Do I want maximum usage? → MIT Do I want patent protection? → Apache 2.0 Do I want code to stay open-source always? → GPL Am I building a library? → LGPL Photo by FlyD on Unsplash ✅ Recommendations For most developers: 🟢 MIT License → Best default choice 🟢 Apache 2.0 → Better for professional projects 🔴 GPL → If you care about open-source enforcement 👉 If you’re unsure, MIT is usually safe and widely accepted 💡 Pro Tips for Using Licenses Always include a LICENSE file in root Add license info in your README Use a consistent license across projects Don’t copy code without checking its license If contributing, respect the original license Consider dual licensing for flexibility 🚀 Final Thoughts Licenses might seem like a small detail, but they define the future of your code. Choosing the right one can boost adoption, protect your work & enable collaboration. So next time you push a repo to GitHub, don’t skip the license, it’s just as important as your code.

title: What is Nmap? A Beginner’s Guide to Network Scanning
author: Chulanka Lakmana Thabrew
description: In today’s digital world, understanding networks is essential for anyone interested in cybersecurity, system administration, or ethical hacking. One of the most powerful and widely used tools for network discovery and security auditing is Nmap (Network Mapper). In this article, we’ll explore what Nmap is, how to install it, what it does, and why it’s an essential tool for tech enthusiasts and professionals. 🚀 What is Nmap? Nmap (Network Mapper) is an open-source tool used for: Network discovery, Security auditing, Port scanning, Service and OS detection Photo by Boitumelo on Unsplash It allows users to scan a network and identify: Active hosts (devices), Open ports, Running services, Operating systems, Security vulnerabilities (to some extent) Created by Gordon Lyon (also known as Fyodor), Nmap has become a standard tool in cybersecurity. ⚙️ How to Install Nmap Installing Nmap is simple, depending on your operating system. 🪟 Windows Visit the official Nmap website Download the installer (.exe) Run the installer and follow the setup wizard You’ll also get Zenmap (GUI version) 🐧 Linux (Ubuntu/Debian) sudo apt update sudo apt install nmap 🍎 macOS Using Homebrew: brew install nmap ✅ Verify Installation nmap --version 🔧 What Does Nmap Do? Nmap is extremely powerful and supports multiple types of scans. Photo by Chris Yang on Unsplash Before performing a scan, we need to know which IP address your machine belongs. 🪟Windows ipconfig 🐧Ubuntu/ Linux ip addr 🍎macOS ifconfig If you know your IP address, then you can, 1. 🔍 Host Discovery Find devices connected to a network: nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24 2. 🚪 Port Scanning Detect open ports on a system: nmap 192.168.1.1 Common ports: 80 → HTTP 443 → HTTPS 22 → SSH 3. 🧠 Service Version Detection nmap -sV 192.168.1.1 Identifies services and versions running on ports. 4. 💻 OS Detection nmap -O 192.168.1.1 Attempts to detect the operating system of the target. 5. ⚡ Aggressive Scan nmap -A 192.168.1.1 Performs: OS detection Version detection Script scanning Traceroute 🎯 Why Do We Need Nmap? Nmap is important for several reasons: Photo by FlyD on Unsplash 🔐 1. Security Auditing Helps identify: Open ports Unnecessary services Potential vulnerabilities (Some) 🌐 2. Network Management System administrators use Nmap to: Monitor network devices Detect unauthorized systems Manage infrastructure 🕵️ 3. Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing Nmap is a core tool in penetration testing: Reconnaissance phase Information gathering Attack surface analysis 🧪 4. Learning Networking If you’re a student, especially in the IT or CSE field, Nmap helps you understand: TCP/IP behavior Ports and protocols Real-world networking ⚠️ Important Note (Ethical Use) Always use Nmap responsibly. Only scan networks you own or have permission to test Unauthorized scanning can be illegal Photo by Nigel Hoare on Unsplash 🏁 Conclusion Nmap is a powerful, flexible, and essential tool for anyone working with networks or cybersecurity. Whether you’re a beginner learning networking or an advanced ethical hacker, mastering Nmap will give you deep insights into how networks operate.

title: I Stopped Coding… and Built an App Anyway (Thanks to AI)
author: Chulanka Lakmana Thabrew
description: Cursor-like tools are changing how developers work, and it’s happening faster than you think. I used to spend hours writing boilerplate, debugging minor errors, and looking up syntax. Last month, I tried something different: 👉 I described what I wanted… and my IDE built it. No, this isn’t hype. This is the new reality of AI-powered development in today's technology landscape. 😓 The Problem With Traditional Coding Let’s be honest, if we use traditional coding, yet: Photo by Kevin Ku on Unsplash You write the same boilerplate again and again Debugging takes longer than building Learning new frameworks = hours of frustration Small mistakes break everything This is the reality of coding we knew. And most developers don’t spend time building ideas , they spend more time on fixing code. That’s exactly what AI coding tools are trying to solve. 🤖 The Shift: From Typing Code → Prompting Code We’re entering a new era where coding looks like this: “Create a REST API with authentication using Node.js” And the IDE just… does it. Photo by Aerps.com on Unsplash Tools leading this shift include: Cursor GitHub Copilot Codeium Google Antigravity Zed & more….. Instead of writing every line manually, You can describe what you want Let AI generate it Refine and guide 👉 Coding becomes just a conversation, not even a tiny task. 🧠 What Makes Cursor Different? We look inside one tool, Cursor. If you use social media or any tech updates, I'm sure you must have heard this name. Cursor was developed by Anysphere, a startup focused on building AI-native developer tools. Unlike traditional tools, Cursor is built as an AI-first IDE. Here’s what it can do: Understand your entire codebase Generate complete features (not just snippets) Refactor multiple files instantly Explain code like a tutor Think of it as: ChatGPT + VS Code combined into one powerful tool. 💻Vibe Coding Vibe computing is a new approach to programming where developers describe ideas in natural language, and Photo by Growtika on Unsplash AI generates, modifies, and manages the code. Instead of focusing on syntax, developers focus on intent and outcomes. It turns coding into a conversational, creative process, making software development faster, more intuitive, and accessible to more people. ⚡ Real Demo: Building a Login API in Minutes Let’s make this practical. I asked simply from Cursor: “Create a simple Express.js API with user registration and login using JWT.” then I got: const express = require("express"); const jwt = require("jsonwebtoken"); const bodyParser = require("body-parser"); const app = express(); app.use(bodyParser.json()); const users = []; app.post("/register", (req, res) => { const { username, password } = req.body; users.push({ username, password }); res.json({ message: "User registered" }); }); app.post("/login", (req, res) => { const { username, password } = req.body; const user = users.find( u => u.username === username && u.password === password ); if (!user) return res.status(401).send("Invalid credentials"); const token = jwt.sign({ username }, "secretKey"); res.json({ token }); }); app.listen(3000, () => console.log("Server running on port 3000")); 😳 What Normally Takes Hours… If we did this using traditional coding, we would need to Setting up Express Writing routes Handling auth logic Debugging errors from boilerplate, but Photo by Tim Gouw on Unsplash 👉 It was done in seconds by Cursor Then I refined it by asking: “Add password hashing and improve security.” Cursor updated the code instantly. 🔥 Cursor vs Other AI Coding Tools Here’s a quick comparison: | Tool | Strength | Weakness | |---------|--------------------------- |-------------------| | Cursor | Full project understanding | Paid | | Copilot | Great inline suggestions | Limited context | | Codeium | Free alternative | Less powerful | 👉 If Copilot is autocomplete… Cursor is autobuild. ⚠️ The Downsides Let’s Be Honest, AI isn’t perfect yet. Here are real concerns: ❌ Generates incorrect or insecure code ❌ Easy to become over-dependent ❌ Junior devs may skip fundamentals ❌ Debugging AI code still requires skill AI doesn’t replace developers, it exposes weak ones and help to bring coding to next generation. 🔮 The Future of Programming We’re moving toward something bigger: Developers → AI supervisors Code → generated, not written IDE → conversation interface Soon, building software may look like: “Build me a scalable e-commerce backend with Stripe integration.” And it just works even without you sitting in front. 🎯 What You Should Do Right Now Photo by Tim Mossholder on Unsplash If you’re a CS student or developer: ✅ Try Cursor for a week ✅ Use AI for repetitive tasks ✅ Always review generated code ✅ Keep learning fundamentals (DSA, system design) 👉 The goal is not to replace coding, but to amplify your coding ability. 🚀 Final Thoughts Coding isn’t dying. It’s evolving. The developers who win in this new era won’t be the fastest typists… They’ll be the best thinkers.

title: Git Mistakes Every Beginner Makes (And How I Learned Them the Hard Way)
author: Chulanka Lakmana Thabrew
description: I still remember the first time Git “broke” my code. Nothing dramatic happened. No error messages. No warning signs. But the code I had in front of me was not the code I thought I had completed. That was the day I realized something uncomfortable: I was using Git, but I didn’t understand it. If you’re a beginner, chances are you’re making the same mistakes I did. Not because you’re careless, but because no one clearly explained the why behind Git. Let’s talk about those mistakes. 1.0 Treating Git Like a Storage System As beginners, many of us think Git is just a place to store code like Google Drive or OneDrive. But Git is not just storage. It’s a version control system. I used to commit only when I felt “done,” like pressing Save in an editor. The Consequences of this are huge commits, no clear project history, and very hard to undo specific changes. When something broke, I had no idea which change caused it. We can fix this. Commit small, logical changes. Each commit should represent one clear idea. When your history is structured, debugging becomes easier because you know exactly where to look. Git becomes powerful when your history tells a story. 2.0 Write meaningless commit messages As beginners, we often treat commit messages as something unimportant. Since Git requires a message, we quickly type final, bug fix, or update. At first, it seems fine. But after a few weeks, when you revisit your code and see multiple commits named “update,” you won’t remember what you updated. Now imagine sharing your repository with someone else. They look at your commit history and learn nothing from it. The Consequences of this are a confusing project history, hard-to-track logic changes, and a poor collaboration experience. We can fix this. Create a simple structure for your commit messages. A good commit message explains what changed and why it changed. Good commit messages turn Git into documentation. 3.0 Committing Without Checking What’s Staged Many beginners simply code and then run, git add . without thinking. This causes debug files to be in commits, temporary files pushed to remote, or embarrassing cleanups later. How can we avoid this problem? For this, the git gives us a tool, git status. We can always run this command before committing. If we do this git gives us visibility, then we can use it. 4.0 Working directly on the main branch. For a long time, I avoided branches because most of my projects were solo. I thought branches were “advanced Git stuff.” But in one project, I committed directly to the main branch after updating the codebase. Minutes later, I realized I had messed up, and there was no clean version to return to. I know most beginners think branches were advanced git stuff, or what I thought. Because of this, there can be many consequences, such as one bad change could break everything, and there is no easy way back. Create branches even when working alone. Branches give you freedom. You can experiment confidently because your main branch remains stable. 5.0 Being Afraid of Merge Conflicts The first time I saw a merge conflict, I thought I had destroyed the repository. But when I slowed down and actually read it, I understood something important: Merge conflicts are not errors. They are conversations. Git is simply asking you which version you want to keep. Avoiding collaboration and learning core git concepts can be a consequence of being afraid when you see a conflict. Don’t panic. Read carefully. Understand both changes. Resolve deliberately. Merge conflicts aren’t the enemy; they are part of real development. The moment Git stopped feeling scary was the moment I stopped trying to memorize commands and started trying to understand consequences. Mistakes are not signs of failure. They’re proof that you’re learning something real. If Git feels confusing today, that’s okay. One day, you’ll look back and realize it was never your enemy. It was your safety net.

title: 20 Movies from 2025 You Shouldn’t Miss
author: Chulanka Lakmana Thabrew
description: Movies in 2025 reminded us why storytelling on the big screen still matters. From visually stunning blockbusters to quiet films that stayed with us long after the credits rolled, this year delivered a wide range of cinematic experiences. Some movies pushed technical boundaries, some explored deep human emotions, and others simply gave us unforgettable entertainment. This list is not based purely on box office numbers or ratings. Instead, it reflects impact, storytelling, performances, creativity, and the way these films connected with audiences. Here are 20 of the best movies released in 2025 that made this year truly special for cinema lovers. 20. Die My Love Die, My Love is an intensely raw, emotionally charged film that immerses viewers in a woman’s inner world of love, identity, and psychological isolation. It excels in creating an unsettling atmosphere through personal storytelling, where silence and subtle expressions speak louder than dialogue. The film explores mental health and relationships without romanticizing pain, making it a thought-provoking watch. It’s ideal for viewers who enjoy slow-burn, character-driven cinema that challenges emotional comfort zones. 19. Marty Supreme Marty Supreme features a charismatic yet flawed character, making the story honest and engaging. The film mixes humor with quiet reflection, gradually revealing Marty’s motivations, insecurities, and ambitions. It allows characters space to breathe, making emotional moments more natural. The film’s memorable balance between entertainment and introspection reveals themes of self-worth, growth, and the costs of success. Though it appears light, it delivers a lasting, thoughtful message. 18. Predator Badlands Predator: Badlands strips the franchise to its most primal elements, centering on survival, instinct, and isolation. Set in a harsh, unforgiving landscape, the environment itself becomes a constant threat, creating tension even in silence. Focusing on atmosphere and suspense over nonstop action, the film lets fear build through pacing and visual storytelling. It feels like a return to the franchise’s roots while still pushing it forward — brutal, grounded, and gripping for both longtime fans and newcomers. 17. K Pop Demon Hunters K-Pop Demon Hunters is a bold, imaginative animated film that blends music, action, and fantasy with vibrant visuals and high-energy performances. Its unapologetic embrace of pop culture makes the world feel lively and modern rather than gimmicky. Beneath the flashy style, the film explores identity, teamwork, and self-belief, showing how strength comes from collaboration. Fun, energetic, and uplifting, it delivers a positive message beneath its colorful surface. 16. Roofman Roofman tells a grounded, quietly compelling story about a man living on the margins of society. Using a slow, observant approach, the film lets the audience gradually understand its protagonist without relying on dramatic twists, building tension through realism and restraint. Its strength lies in atmosphere and detail, subtly exploring isolation, survival, and personal morality. Intimate and character-driven, Roofman resonates through reflection rather than spectacle. 15. Fantastic Four: The First Steps Fantastic Four: The First Steps reintroduces Marvel’s first family with a renewed focus on relationships, teamwork, and emotional connection rather than nonstop action. This grounded approach makes the story feel more personal within the larger superhero universe. Balancing science fiction with human emotion, the film weaves themes of responsibility, discovery, and family into its narrative. While it delivers the expected spectacle, it’s at its best when it slows down and lets its characters shine. 14. Weapons Weapons establishes unease from its opening moments, relying on atmosphere and psychological tension rather than easy scares. Through silence, framing, and restrained performances, the film lets dread build gradually as its mystery unfolds. At its core, it explores fear, loss, and the unknown, using layered storytelling that invites interpretation. Weapons stands out as a horror film that values mood and meaning over shock value. 13. Mickey 17 Mickey 17 is a thought-provoking sci-fi film that uses dark humor and repetition to explore identity and human expendability. Its concept-driven story raises questions about individuality, purpose, and what it means to be human. Beyond its premise, the film offers sharp social commentary on technology, labor, and morality. Both entertaining and intellectually stimulating, Mickey 17 stands out as one of the year’s more distinctive films. 12. Thunderbolts, aka New Avengers Thunderbolts, aka New Avengers, shifts the superhero focus from idealism to morally complex anti-heroes, delivering a darker, more grounded tone than typical Marvel entries. This approach adds a refreshing sense of unpredictability. Exploring themes of trust, redemption, and personal conflict, the film thrives on character tension and unstable group dynamics. Rather than relying solely on large-scale action, Thunderbolts stands out through its flawed, compelling characters. 11. Ze Sha 2 Ne Zha 2 builds confidently on the emotional and mythological core of the first film, with grander animation, sharper action, and higher stakes. Blending traditional mythology with a modern tone, it feels both culturally rich and widely relatable. Centered on destiny and personal choice, the story shifts Ne Zha’s journey toward responsibility and growth. This added emotional depth elevates the film beyond spectacle, making it one of the year’s most impactful animated releases. 10. The Long Walk The Long Walk presents a haunting, minimalistic vision of a dystopian future, using repetition and endurance to build intense psychological tension. As the journey continues, the physical struggle becomes a symbol of mental and emotional collapse. Beyond survival, the film explores control, sacrifice, and human desperation, with slow pacing that lets every decision weigh heavily. Emotionally exhausting and deeply effective, The Long Walk shows how fear and authority can reshape human behavior. 9. Frankenstein Frankenstein (2025) reimagines the classic tale with a darker, emotionally layered approach, focusing less on pure horror and more on creation, responsibility, and the cost of human ambition. Its heavy, moody atmosphere highlights the clash between science and morality. The film stands out through its emotional depth, portraying the monster as a tragic figure shaped by rejection and fear. By prioritizing character over shock, Frankenstein feels both timeless and relevant, a thoughtful reinterpretation of a legendary story. 8. Mission Impossible: The Final Reckoning The Final Reckoning brings the Mission: Impossible saga to a dramatic, emotional turning point, raising the stakes from the opening moments with intense action and a strong narrative drive. Every mission feels personal, adding urgency and a sense of finality. Beyond the spectacle, the film reflects on loyalty, sacrifice, and legacy, balancing high-octane thrills with quieter moments of reflection. As a conclusion, it honors the franchise’s history while delivering a powerful and satisfying send-off. 7. Superman Superman (2025) redefines the iconic hero by emphasizing compassion, responsibility, and moral integrity over sheer power. Its hopeful tone grounds Superman’s strength in humanity rather than dominance. By focusing on relationships and inner conflict, the film presents a sincere struggle between personal identity and global responsibility. This take reminds us why Superman endures — not because he is invincible, but because he chooses to do good. 6. Wake Up the Dead Man Wake Up Dead Man continues the Knives Out tradition with sharp dialogue, clever misdirection, and a tightly constructed mystery that keeps every conversation meaningful. Its fresh setting adds a new flavor while staying true to the franchise’s roots. What elevates the film is its character-driven humor and pointed social commentary. Beneath the mystery lies a critique of power, truth, and perception, proving that modern whodunits can be both entertaining and intellectually engaging. 5. Zootopia 2 Zootopia 2 expands its vibrant world with new districts and characters while retaining the humor and heart that made the original so beloved. The animation remains colorful and expressive, appealing to all ages. At its core, the sequel explores cooperation, prejudice, and personal growth through Judy and Nick’s evolving journey. Both entertaining and thoughtful, Zootopia 2 works as a fun adventure and a meaningful continuation of the story. 4. One Battle After Another One Battle After Another takes a grounded approach to conflict, focusing on emotional consequences rather than heroic action. Its raw tone and reflective pacing portray struggle as ongoing and exhausting. By exploring internal battles alongside physical ones, the film sensitively addresses trauma, loss, and moral conflict. Challenging but deeply human, it rewards viewers who appreciate thoughtful, character-driven cinema. 3. Avatar: Fire and Ash Avatar: Fire and Ash expands Pandora with darker themes, richer emotions, and breathtaking new environments that fully immerse the audience. The scale remains vast, pushing visual storytelling to new heights. Beyond spectacle, the film leans into conflict, power, and moral ambiguity, making character choices feel heavier and more consequential. It shows the Avatar series evolving with deeper, more mature storytelling. 2. F1 Movie F1 delivers a high-speed cinematic experience that captures the intensity and pressure of professional racing. Blending technical realism with dramatic storytelling, every race sequence feels precise, dangerous, and immersive. Beyond the track, the film explores rivalry, ambition, and personal redemption, highlighting the sacrifices required to compete at the highest level. More than a sports film, F1 is a human story about obsession and resilience. 1. Sinners Sinners is a tense, atmospheric thriller that builds unease through mood, symbolism, and restrained performances rather than overt scares. Its dark tone sustains a lingering sense of discomfort throughout. Exploring guilt, morality, and the consequences of hidden choices, the film challenges viewers to question who the real villains are. Prioritizing psychological depth over shock, Sinners is both unsettling and memorable. Looking back, 2025 was a powerful year for films. It showed that cinema can still surprise us, challenge our thinking, and bring people together through shared stories. Whether it was a thought-provoking drama, an imaginative sci-fi journey, or a heartfelt animation, each movie on this list left its own mark. Of course, every viewer experiences movies differently. This is my take on the best of 2025, and I’m sure your list might look a little different. 👉 Which movie from 2025 was your favorite? Let me know in the comments, and feel free to share any films you think deserved a spot on this list.

title: Understanding Iterators, Generators, and Decorators in Python
author: Chulanka Lakmana Thabrew
description: The first time I saw the word “yield” in Python code, I was surprised. Because I assumed that was a typo, I neglected it and moved forward. But last week, when I was refering a course material, I saw that word again. Then I got curious to get to know about that yield and what it does in code. I try to search in google about the word yield. In that search, I found three new terms of python language: iterators, generators, and decorators. Many Python developers write loops, functions, and utilities every day but still feel unsure when terms like iterator, generator, or decorator appear in discussions or interviews. These concepts often sound complex, yet they quietly power some of Python’s most elegant features. I was no different. I could write working Python code, but I didn’t truly understand why certain patterns existed or how Python handled them internally. Once I connected these ideas, Python started to feel less like a collection of syntax rules and more like a thoughtfully designed language. Iterators: The Silent Workers When you were coding, you definitely used for or while loops. Every for loop tells a small story, one item at a time. We consider a simple for loop. numbers = [1, 2, 3] for n in numbers: print(n) In here, behind the scenes, Python creates an iterator. An iterator is simply an object that remembers where it is while looping. For the above simple code, this is the iterator that was created. iterator = iter(numbers) print(next(iterator)) # output 1 We can implement iterators manually as below. numbers = [1, 2, 3] iterator = iter(numbers) print(next(iterator)) # output 1 print(next(iterator)) # output 2 print(next(iterator)) # output 3 Additionally, we can provide a custom iterator example as follows. class CountUp: def __init__(self, max): self.num = 0 self.max = max def __iter__(self): return self def __next__(self): if self.num >= self.max: raise StopIteration self.num += 1 return self.num counter = CountUp(3) for n in counter: print(n) 💡 Key Point: Iterators use __iter__() and __next__(). Generators: Iterators with a Memory-Saving Mindset You’ve probably seen loops that run thousands or even millions of times. This makes the codebase very memory-heavy. def squares(n): result = [] for i in range(n): result.append(i * i) return result # n = 10**10 But you know, there is a method to release this heavy workload. This is called as generators. def squares(n): for i in range(n): yield i * i The yield keyword pauses execution and resumes later, making generators ideal for large or infinite data streams. Just like list comprehensions, but we use them with ( ) instead of [ ].In here, no lists, no storage, just values flowing one by one. squares = (i * i for i in range(5)) for s in squares: print(s) Decorators: Enhancing Behavior Without Touching the Core First time I saw decorators, Decorators felt mysterious until I realized they were just functions wrapping other functions. def logger(func): def wrapper(): print("Function started") func() print("Function ended") return wrapper @logger def greet(): print("Hello!") Decorators are simply used to change the functionality of a function, without changing its code structure. This allows us to extend behavior without modifying existing code, a powerful idea in clean software design. Let's see how we can do this step by step. Step 01: a normal function def greet(): print("Hello") Step 2: A decorator function def my_greeting(func): def wrapper(): print("Before the function runs") func() print("After the function runs") return wrapper Step 3: Apply decorator @my_greeting def greet(): print("Hello") # output """ Before the function runs Hello After the function runs """ The @my_decorator line is just syntax sugar for greet = my_greeting(greet). Now I'd like to explain more how this works because I think decorator is a little bit more difficult than the other two. Not difficult, just a little more than the other two. First python sees @my_decorator. and it passes greet into my_decorator. Then my_decorator returns wrapper, and greet now points to wrapper. So when we call greet(), we are actually calling wrapper(). At first glance, all three of iterators, generators, and decorators can feel like advanced Python concepts reserved for later stages of learning. I felt that hesitation too. But once I took the time to understand them, I realized something important: I had already been using them, I just wasn’t aware of it. Iterators explain how Python moves through data. Generators show how Python does that efficiently. Decorators reveal how Python allows behavior to be extended without rewriting existing code. Together, they form a quiet foundation beneath much of what we write every day. Understanding these ideas didn’t make my Python code longer or more complex. It made it more intentional. Now, when I see a for loop, a yield, or a @decorator, I don’t see mystery anymore; I see design. And that shift, from writing Python to understanding Python, is what makes learning the language truly rewarding.
